human_tolerance.notes: Judgement: broad natural and pastoral habitat use does not establish urban affinity; adapter is a conservative simulation classification, with roads treated as a major risk.

phases.name: territorial
phases.note: The species remains active year-round; seasonal changes in emergence and grazing timing are not represented as calendar month gates.

external.note: Usage key and taxon ID read from the respective provider records; both resolve the accepted species Vombatus ursinus at species rank (checked 2026-10-31).

common_names.note: iNaturalist preferred common name is Bare-nosed Wombat; the Annual Review uses the same common name.

range.note: The review describes the species as fauna from southeast Australia and records continental and continental-island subspeciation; the country-level native range is recorded as AU only.

traits.body_plan.note: The review describes the wombat as quadrupedal.

traits.limb_count.note: Four limbs, consistent with the review's quadrupedal description.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: The review describes slow ground movement while feeding and reports that observed maximum running speeds may be closer to 20 km/h, while explicitly noting that no literature supports the commonly repeated 40 km/h figure. Walk is represented for feeding; Gallop is an authored short-burst escape gait mapping, not a measured gait or speed. Burrowing has no built-in pose.

traits.skin.note: The review describes a coarse fur coat.

traits.flight.note: Terrestrial quadrupedal marsupial; no flight capability described.

traits.respiration.note: Mammal; lungs are represented from the stated class.

traits.metamorphosis.note: Marsupial development has no metamorphic stage.

traits.nest_type.note: Fossorial; uses burrows for shelter and sleep.

traits.perching.note: Ground-dwelling quadruped with no perching behavior described.

traits.size_class.note: Medium follows the 28 kg modeled adult mass, within the review's adult range of 17–39 kg and the schema's 1–50 kg Medium class.

traits.mass_kg.note: The review reports adult masses of 17–39 kg across subspecies. 28 kg is the midpoint of that published range, used as a typical adult proxy because no species-wide mean is given.

traits.mass_range_kg.note: The review gives an adult mass range of 17–39 kg across subspecies.

traits.length_m.note: The review gives adult lengths of 77–115 cm. 0.96 m is the midpoint of that body-length range; the schema measures nose to tail, and the vestigial tail is about 25 mm, so 0.98 m is used as an approximate nose-to-tail value.

traits.lifespan_y.note: The review says typical lifespan is perceived to be 10–15 years but has not been demonstrated rigorously. 12.5 years is the midpoint of that stated typical range; this is a low-confidence proxy, not a measured mean or maximum.

traits.diet.note: The review says diet is dominated by native grasses, with other plant foods also eaten. The 0.95 graze / 0.05 browse split is an authored simulation allocation, not measured dietary proportions.

traits.social.note: The review describes a solitary species. Group size is set to one; temporary asynchronous use of shared burrow systems is not represented as a social group.

traits.activity_pattern.note: The review describes nocturnal activity, with emergence commonly in late afternoon and seasonal variation in emergence times; represented as crepuscular.

traits.defense.note: Retreat into burrows is a documented refuge behavior; Hide represents that response.

traits.wariness.note: Judgement: 0.6 represents a solitary burrow-dweller that retreats to shelter when disturbed; no numeric wariness estimate is available.

habitat.use.note: Ground grazing and fossorial burrow use are documented; 0.8 ground / 0.2 fossorial is an authored placement split, not measured time budget.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Burrows are described as shelter, sleep sites, predator refuge and thermal refuge.

habitat.resources.note: The review describes native grasses as the dominant diet, other plant foods in smaller amounts, and burrow use. Resource weights follow the authored dietary allocation.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: Judgement: pasture use supports an Adapter classification at broad scale, while a low impervious ceiling, high road mortality and no garden use avoid claiming urban dependence.

seasonal.strategy.note: The review documents activity throughout the year and seasonal variation in emergence timing, rather than hibernation or migration.

seasonal.phases.note: A single year-round active phase avoids importing local month boundaries. Seasonal variation in emergence timing is not represented as month-gated behavior.

seasonal.life_stages.note: The review describes juvenile development and adult life history; durations are omitted because no single general duration is assigned here.

behavior.note: Shared ground-forager FSM with grass grazing mapped to the graze resource, walking movement, and daytime rest at the burrow shelter. It approximates nocturnal/crepuscular feeding via daylight shelter; it cannot animate digging or burrow entry.

look.note: Judgement informed by the review's thick-set, low-slung, barrel-shaped form, broad head, short strong neck, vestigial tail, coarse fur and variable brown-to-gray pelage. The 0.025 tail ratio reflects the approximately 25 mm tail relative to a roughly 1 m body. The block model is stylized.

traits.shoulder_height_m.note: The review reports adult height of approximately 22–25 cm; 0.235 m is the midpoint of that approximate range.
